correctness.rationale: Hanada–Lentfer–Vindas-Meléndez Prop 3.4 gives vertex layers with k entries 1 and shifted tail lambda_j=a-1+jb. After translation by -1 and symmetry, unique minimax center equals s 1_n with layer distances Q_k(s)=ns^2-2S_k s+T_k; adjacent differences lambda_k(lambda_k-2s) ensure one active layer or two neighbors. D_k=2S_k-n lambda_(k-1) is strictly decreasing with difference -2(a-1)-b(2k+n); first K satisfying D_K<=nb and boundary cases yield claimed center/radius and contacts, accounting for coincident layers k=0,1 at a=1. Independent rational arithmetic tested 576 triples 2<=n<=10,1<=a,b<=8, checking the minmax against ALL breakpoints and stationary candidates and verifying contact adjacency after collapsing equal layers. Classical K_n formula and golden-ratio limit follow exact quadratic inequality; not a numerical asymptotic extrapolation.
residual_risks: n>=2 integer a,b>=1; ordinary Euclidean metric and canonical family, not arbitrary positive parameter vectors or affine invariance.
